newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Elephants kill at least 50 a year in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Elephants kill at least 50 a year in Sri Lanka.

text.p: Elephants kill at least 50 people every year in Sri Lanka as forest cover shrinks and the animals are forced out of the jungles, the state-owned Daily News said on Sunday.
The newspaper quoted wildlife officials as saying more men were killed by wild elephants than women in encounters that took place mostly at night.
They said the growing problem was mostly due to a rapidly growing human population and shrinking forest cover.
A survey in 1993 showed that Sri Lanka had an estimated 2,000 elephants in the wild. The newspaper quoted officials as saying many elephants had been killed by farmers guarding their crops.
Sri Lanka has several elephants in captivity, mostly at Buddhist temples where they are used for religious ceremonies.
